headline: I could not do (2) and (3): a third instance cannot exist while the resident runs. This is not a guess and not a restatement of j5's r10t1 - I verified it three ways myself. In code, start() returns early for an identical implementation before --force is even consulted (dsh-eda-bridge.mjs L612-617 vs L618), and there is no port environment variable anywhere in the binary. On the wire, 'node dsh-eda-bridge.mjs' and 'node dsh-eda-bridge.mjs --force' both printed 'Bridge server is already running on port 49620; no new instance started.' and both exited 0, while 49621/49622/49623 stayed closed before and after. Architecturally, even a forced second HTTP listener could never receive a registration: the editor's built-in gateway dials the hard-coded ws://127.0.0.1:49630, the resident holds 49630 (TCP connect succeeded before and after), and t53's discover() walks 49620..49630 in order and returns the first connected instance with no way to name a port. So the honest outcome is blocked. What I did do is take a read-only resident reading at 14:35:32.448Z (exit 0, 5/5, 21/8/13/55/55/2) and label it as resident-only, not as third-instance evidence.

step6_N1PatchSuggestion.context: N1 from r9t7: running the runbook's 3.3 probe without 3.1 first silently probes whichever tab is bound. A wrong tab fails closed (manual.visible=false) but the only hint is the url field, so a reader can mistake it for 'the landing page says not visible'.
step6_N1PatchSuggestion.owner: j5 maintains the runbook file; I am only supplying text, and I did not edit it

requirementA_throws.requirement: the guard must throw and stop the flow, not return a boolean for the caller to interpret
requirementA_throws.howItThrows: the JS guard is the first statement of the eval, so a mismatch aborts the whole eval: dpx reports exit 1 / status error, and the runbook cannot proceed to the click step. The PowerShell guard throws in the operator shell for the same reason.
requirementA_throws.liveProof: with $RelayPort substituted to 49621 while the bound tab was http://127.0.0.1:49620/landing, dpx eval returned exit 1, status "error", code "JS_FAILED", and the underlying exception was "Error: WRONG_PAGE: http://127.0.0.1:49620/landing is not http://127.0.0.1:49621/landing" at 2026-10-24T14:43:52.789Z - so the failure interrupts rather than handing back a flag

requirementB_exactMatch.requirement: no StartsWith-style prefix test; compare normalised origin+path for exact equality, and explain why a prefix test is unsafe
requirementB_exactMatch.normalisation: parse both URLs, then compare protocol + host + pathname with trailing slashes removed; query and hash are dropped, because /landing?x=1#y is still the landing page
requirementB_exactMatch.whyPrefixIsUnsafe: a prefix test on 'http://127.0.0.1:49620/landing' accepts every URL that merely begins with that string. I measured it: startsWith returned true for /landing, for /landing-evil and for /landing.html. So a page at /landing-evil - a different document that this guard would treat as the landing page - would be accepted and probed. Exact equality after normalisation rejects both, which is why I do not use StartsWith.
requirementB_exactMatch.counterexampleProof: in the 8-case harness the guard threw for /landing-evil and for /landing.html, so the prefix hole is actually closed rather than argued away

requirementC_portParameterized.requirement: 49620 must not be hardcoded; use the runbook variables $RelayPort/$LandingUrl, and show that 49621 does not get falsely rejected
requirementC_portParameterized.jsSide: the port is a token, not a literal: the template carries @@RELAY_PORT@@ and the runbook substitutes it from $RelayPort before eval, so the expected URL is built from the configured port. The numeric token avoids quoting problems entirely.
requirementC_portParameterized.psSide: $RelayPort is the single source; $LandingUrl = "http://127.0.0.1:$RelayPort/landing" is derived from it, exactly as in runbook section 0.1
requirementC_portParameterized.noFalseRejectAt49621: harness case "expected 49621 / parameterized must NOT reject" passed: with the port set to 49621, http://127.0.0.1:49621/landing is accepted rather than rejected. The live run also shows the port is honoured dynamically - the same page was accepted under 49620 and rejected under 49621, so the guard reads the configured port instead of a baked-in constant.

step6_N1PatchSuggestion.whyBothVersionsAgree: both blocks now normalise the same way (protocol + host + pathname, trailing slashes trimmed, query/hash dropped) and both throw on mismatch. The paste tests confirm they agree at the level that matters: the accepting case returns PASS / EVAL_OK with exit 0, and the landing-evil case throws WRONG_PAGE on both sides with a non-zero exit.
